public_rationale: NHTSA's February 16, 2022 notice opened an investigation after receiving 354 complaints over the preceding nine months alleging unexpected braking in 2021–2022 Tesla Model 3 and Model Y vehicles [e1]. The notice does not establish the cause of the reported braking or assess vision-only neural systems against Level 5 requirements [e1]. This evidence does not settle whether neural systems available by February 25, 2022 lacked the capabilities required for reliable vision-only Level 5 driving [e1].
limitations: The complaints are allegations, not completed technical findings.
The packet contains neither a representative capability assessment of contemporary vision-only neural systems nor a qualifying Level 5 demonstration.
The evidence does not independently measure cognitive depth or attribute the reported braking to neural-system limitations.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Current neural networks lack the cognitive depth and robustness needed for reliable Level 5 self-driving from vision alone.

statement.excerpt: Current neural nets lack the cognitive depth and robustness that would be necessary to support reliable L5 self-driving form vision alone.
statement.document_title: The New Sport of Misrepresenting AI Criticism

from_speaker: lack the cognitive depth and robustness
necessary to support reliable L5 self-driving
our_interpretation: Current refers to the quoted February 25, 2022 statement, not systems available in September 2022 or at evaluation.
The target is the February 2022 capability state through the tweet date, using that month's public records for this ongoing observation.
L5 means full driving automation across the driving conditions covered by that level, without requiring a supervising driver.
The plain reading concerns insufficient capability and robustness in contemporary vision-only neural systems. It is stronger than the observation that no qualifying product had been deployed.
Cognitive depth has no independent measurement here; the capability assessment must rely on demonstrated driving performance and diagnosed limitations.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous evaluations of relevant vision-only neural systems establish perception or decision-making limitations that prevent reliable Level 5 operation. Mere nondeployment or one manufacturer's failure is insufficient to establish the whole claim.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A documented system using neural networks and vision alone demonstrates reliable Level 5 operation with the technology available by February 25, 2022.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Representative evaluations of vision-only neural systems available by February 25, 2022 that establish limitations preventing reliable Level 5 operation, or a validated Level 5 demonstration using technology available by that date. Evaluations must identify sensor configurations, operating conditions, interventions, failure rates and causes.
